exact_statement: For the class f_w(u)=1[u=w], w in [n]^d, over Q, the minimal Hankel rank is d+1. A single exact full-matrix query of dimension d+1 can identify w with polynomial input and output bit cost while satisfying sum_i X_i^T X_i <= I. In the adaptive full-matrix Gaussian oracle of the N25 card, any zero-vs-hidden-word test with both errors <= delta and per-query excitation cap E=1 has expected total query dimension C >= 2 sigma^2 n^d kl(1-delta,delta); expected returned-entry count is at least C.
assumptions: full matrix output, independent Gaussian noise with variance sigma^2 in every real entry
each query tuple satisfies sum_i X_i^T X_i <= I
C is expected sum of query matrix dimensions under the zero target
the noisy learner distinguishes zero from every f_w with both errors at most delta < 1/2
novelty_boundary: This is a strict interface counterexample to naive exact-to-noisy transfer for a finite hidden-word subclass. It does not refute L01 or prove priority; exact weighted-automaton learning, noisy spectral learning, tolerance-based active automata, and adaptive Gaussian sensing all have prior art.

costs.exact_decode_runtime: polynomial in n,d and bit length using the known prime table
costs.noisy_expected_total_dimension_lower_bou: 2 sigma^2 (n/E)^d kl(1-delta,delta), with E=1 in the separation instance
costs.noisy_expected_returned_entries_lower_bo: same lower bound because D^2 >= D

falsifier: An admissible adaptive Gaussian strategy with both testing errors <= delta and expected total query dimension below the displayed bound, or a collision in the exact prime-position encoding, would refute the claim.
